verses.first: For innumerable troubles are come about me; my ſins have taken ſuch hold upon me that I am not able to look up
verses.second: yea, they are more in number than the hairs of my head, and my heart hath failed me.

verses.first: O Lord, let it be thy pleaſure to deliver me
verses.second: make haſte, O Lord, to help me.

verses.first: Let them be aſhamed and confounded together, that ſeek after my ſoul to deſtroy it
verses.second: let them be driven backward and put to rebuke, that wiſh me evil.

verses.first: Let them be deſolate, and rewarded with ſhame
verses.second: that ſay unto me, Fie upon thee, fie upon thee.

verses.first: Let all thoſe that ſeek thee be joyful and glad in thee
verses.second: and let ſuch as love thy ſalvation ſay alway, The Lord be praiſed.

verses.first: As for me, I am poor and needy
verses.second: but the Lord careth for me.

verses.first: Thou art my helper and redeemer
verses.second: make no long tarrying, O my God.

verses.first: BLESSED is he that conſidereth the poor and needy
verses.second: the Lord ſhall deliver him in the time of trouble.

verses.first: The Lord preſerve him, and keep him alive, that he may be bleſſed upon earth
verses.second: and deliver not thou him into the will of his enemies.

verses.first: The Lord comfort him, when he lieth ſick upon his bed
verses.second: make thou all his bed in his ſickneſs.

verses.first: I ſaid, Lord, be merciful unto me
verses.second: heal my ſoul, for I have ſinned againſt thee.

verses.first: Mine enemies ſpeak evil of me
verses.second: When ſhall he die, and his name periſh?

verses.first: And if he come to ſee me, he ſpeaketh vanity
verses.second: and his heart conceiveth falſhood within himſelf, and when he cometh forth he telleth it.

verses.first: All mine enemies whiſper together againſt me
verses.second: even againſt me do they imagine this evil.

verses.first: Let the ſentence of guiltineſs proceed againſt him
verses.second: and now that he lieth, let him riſe up no more.

verses.first: Yea, even mine own familiar friend, whom I truſted
verses.second: who did alſo eat of my bread, hath laid great wait for me.

verses.first: But be thou merciful unto me, O Lord
verses.second: raiſe thou me up again, and I ſhall reward them.

verses.first: By this I know thou favoureſt me
verses.second: that mine enemy doth not triumph againſt me.

verses.first: And when I am in my health, thou upholdeſt me
verses.second: and ſhalt ſet me before thy face for ever.

verses.first: Bleſſed be the Lord God of Iſrael
verses.second: world without end. Amen.

verses.first: LIKE as the hart deſireth the water-brooks
verses.second: ſo longeth my ſoul after thee, O God.

verses.first: My ſoul is athirſt for God, yea, even for the living God
verses.second: when ſhall I come to appear before the preſence of God?

verses.first: My tears have been my meat day and night
verses.second: while they daily ſay unto me, Where is now thy God?

verses.first: Now when I think thereupon, I pour out my heart by myſelf
verses.second: for I went with the multitude, and brought them forth into the houſe of God;

verses.first: In the voice of praiſe and thankſgiving
verses.second: among ſuch as keep holy-day.

verses.first: Why art thou ſo full of heavineſs, O my ſoul
verses.second: and why art thou ſo diſquieted within me?

verses.first: Put thy truſt in God
verses.second: for I will yet give him thanks for the help of his countenance.

verses.first: My God, my ſoul is vexed within me
verses.second: therefore will I remember thee concerning the land of Jordan, and the little hill of Hermon.

verses.first: One deep calleth another, becauſe of the noiſe of the water-pipes
verses.second: all thy waves and ſtorms are gone over me.

verses.first: The Lord hath granted his loving-kindneſs in the day-time
verses.second: and in the nightſeaſon did I ſing of him, and made my prayer unto the God of my life.

verses.first: I will ſay unto the God of my ſtrength, Why haſt thou forgotten me
verses.second: why go I thus heavily, while the enemy oppreſſeth me?

verses.first: My bones are ſmitten aſunder as with a ſword
verses.second: while mine enemies that trouble me caſt me in the teeth;

verses.first: Namely, while they ſay daily unto me
verses.second: Where is now thy God?

verses.first: Why art thou ſo vexed, O my ſoul
verses.second: and why art thou ſo diſquieted within me?

verses.first: O put thy truſt in God
verses.second: for I will yet thank him, which is the help of my countenance, and my God.

verses.first: GIVE ſentence with me, O God, and defend my cauſe againſt the ungodly people
verses.second: O deliver me from the deceitful and wicked man.

verses.first: For thou art the God of my ſtrength, why haſt thou put me from thee
verses.second: and why go I ſo heavily, while the enemy oppreſſeth me?

verses.first: O ſend out thy light and thy truth, that they may lead me
verses.second: and bring me unto thy holy hill, and to thy dwelling.

verses.first: And that I may go unto the altar of God, even unto the God of my joy and gladneſs
verses.second: and upon the harp I will give thanks unto thee, O God, my God.

verses.first: Why art thou ſo heavy, O my ſoul
verses.second: and why art thou ſo diſquieted within me?

verses.first: O put thy truſt in God
verses.second: for I will yet give him thanks, which is the help of my countenance, and my God.

verses.first: WE have heard with our ears, O God, our fathers have told us
verses.second: what thou haſt done in their time of old;

verses.first: How thou haſt driven out the heathen with thy hand, and planted them in
verses.second: how thou haſt deſtroyed the nations and caſt them out.

verses.first: For they gat not the land in poſſeſſion through their own ſword
verses.second: neither was it their own arm that helped them;

verses.first: But thy right hand, and thine arm, and the light of thy countenance
verses.second: becauſe thou hadſt a favour unto them.

verses.first: Thou art my King, O God
verses.second: ſend help unto Jacob.

verses.first: Through thee will we overthrow our enemies
verses.second: and in thy Name will we tread them under, that riſe up againſt us.

verses.first: For I will not truſt in my bow
verses.second: it is not my ſword that ſhall help me;

verses.first: But it is thou that ſaveſt us from our enemies
verses.second: and putteſt them to confuſion that hate us.

verses.first: We make our boaſt of God all day long
verses.second: and will praiſe thy Name for ever.

verses.first: But now thou art far off, and putteſt us to confuſion
verses.second: and goeſt not forth with our armies.

verses.first: Thou makeſt us to turn our backs upon our enemies
verses.second: ſo that they which hate us ſpoil our goods.

verses.first: Thou letteſt us be eaten up like ſheep
verses.second: and haſt ſcattered us among the heathen.

verses.first: Thou ſelleſt thy people for nought
verses.second: and takeſt no money for them.

verses.first: Thou makeſt us to be rebuked of our neighbours
verses.second: to be laughed to ſcorn, and had in deriſion of them that are round about us.

verses.first: Thou makeſt us to be a by-word among the heathen
verses.second: and that the people ſhake their heads at us.

verses.first: My confuſion is daily before me
verses.second: and the ſhame of my face hath covered me;

verses.first: For the voice of the ſlanderer and blaſphemer
verses.second: for the enemy and avenger.

verses.first: And though all this be come upon us, yet do we not forget thee
verses.second: nor behave ourſelves frowardly in thy covenant.

verses.first: Our heart is not turned back
verses.second: neither our ſteps gone out of thy way;

verses.first: No, not when thou haſt ſmitten us into the place of dragons
verses.second: and covered us with the ſhadow of death.

verses.first: If we have forgotten the Name of our God, and holden up our hands to any ſtrange god
verses.second: ſhall not God ſearch it out? for he knoweth the very ſecrets of the heart.

verses.first: For thy ſake alſo are we killed all the day long
verses.second: and are counted as ſheep appointed to be ſlain.

verses.first: Up, Lord, why ſleepeſt thou
verses.second: awake, and be not abſent from us for ever.

verses.first: Wherefore hideſt thou thy face
verses.second: and forgetteſt our miſery and trouble?

verses.first: For our ſoul is brought low, even unto the duſt
verses.second: our belly cleaveth unto the ground.

verses.first: Ariſe, and help us
verses.second: and deliver us for thy mercy’s ſake.

verses.first: MY heart is inditing of a good matter
verses.second: I ſpeak of the thing which I have made unto the King.

verses.first: My tongue is the pen
verses.second: of a ready writer.

verses.first: Thou art fairer than the children of men
verses.second: full of grace are thy lips, becauſe God hath bleſſed thee for ever.

verses.first: Gird thee with thy ſword upon thy thigh, O thou moſt Mighty
verses.second: according to thy worſhip and renown.

verses.first: Good luck have thou with thine honour
verses.second: ride on, becauſe of the word of truth, of meekneſs, and righteouſneſs; and thy right hand ſhall teach thee terrible things.

verses.first: Thy arrows are very ſharp, and the people ſhall be ſubdued unto thee
verses.second: even in the midſt among the King’s enemies.

verses.first: Thy ſeat, O God, endureth for ever
verses.second: the ſceptre of thy kingdom is a right ſceptre.

verses.first: Thou haſt loved righteouſneſs, and hated iniquity
verses.second: wherefore God, even thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladneſs above thy fellows.

verses.first: All thy garments ſmell of myrrh, aloes, and caſſia
verses.second: out of the ivory palaces, whereby they have made thee glad.

verses.first: Kings daughters were among thy honourable women
verses.second: upon thy right hand did ſtand the queen in a veſture of gold, wrought about with divers colours.

verses.text: Hearken, O daughter, and conſider, incline thine ear; forget alſo thine own people, and thy father's houſe.

verses.first: So ſhall the King have pleaſure in thy beauty
verses.second: for his is thy Lord God, and worſhip thou him.

verses.first: And the daughter of Tyre ſhall be there with a gift
verses.second: like as the rich alſo among the people ſhall make their ſupplication before thee.

verses.first: The King’s daughter is all glorious within
verses.second: her clothing is of wrought gold.

verses.first: She ſhall be brought unto the King in raiment of needle-work
verses.second: the virgins that be her fellows ſhall bear her company, and ſhall be brought unto thee.

verses.first: With joy and gladneſs ſhall they be brought
verses.second: and ſhall enter into the King’s palace.

verses.first: Inſtead of thy fathers thou ſhalt have children
verses.second: whom thou mayeſt make princes in all lands.

verses.first: I will remember thy Name from one generation to another
verses.second: therefore ſhall the people give thanks unto thee, world without end.

verses.first: GOD is our hope and ſtrength
verses.second: a very preſent help in trouble.

verses.first: Therefore will we not fear, though the earth be moved
verses.second: and though the hills be carried into the midſt of the ſea;

verses.first: Though the waters thereof rage and ſwell
verses.second: and though the mountains ſhake at the tempeſt of the ſame.

verses.first: The rivers of the flood thereof ſhall make glad the city of God
verses.second: the holy place of the tabernacle of the moſt Higheſt.

verses.first: God is in the midſt of her, therefore ſhall ſhe not be removed
verses.second: God ſhall help her, and that right early.

verses.first: The heathen make much ado, and the kingdoms are moved
verses.second: but God hath ſhewed his voice, and the earth ſhall melt away.

verses.first: The Lord of hoſts is with us
verses.second: the God of Jacob is our refuge.

verses.first: O come hither, and behold the works of the Lord
verses.second: what deſtruction he hath brought upon the earth.

verses.first: He maketh wars to ceaſe in all the world
verses.second: he breaketh the bow, and knappeth the ſpear in ſunder, and burneth the chariots in the fire.

verses.first: Be ſtill then, and know that I am God
verses.second: I will be exalted among the heathen, and I will be exalted in the earth.

verses.first: The Lord of hoſts is with us
verses.second: the God of Jacob is our refuge.

verses.first: O Clap your hand together, all ye people
verses.second: O ſing unto God with the voice of melody.

verses.first: For the Lord is high, and to be feared
verses.second: he is the great King upon all the earth.

verses.first: He ſhall ſubdue the people under us
verses.second: and the nations under our feet.

verses.first: He ſhall chooſe out an heritage for us
verses.second: even the worſhip of Jacob, whom he loved.

verses.first: God is gone up with a merry noiſe
verses.second: and the Lord with the ſound of the trump.

verses.first: O ſing praiſes, ſing praiſes unto our God
verses.second: O ſing praiſes, ſing praiſes unto our King.

verses.first: For God is the King of all the earth
verses.second: ſing ye praiſes with underſtanding.

verses.first: God reigneth over the heathen
verses.second: God ſitteth upon his holy ſeat.

verses.first: The princes of the people are joined unto the people of the God of Abraham
verses.second: for God, which is very high exalted, doth defend the earth, as it were with a ſhield.

verses.first: GREAT is the Lord, and highly to be praiſed
verses.second: in the city of our God, even upon his holy hill.

verses.first: The hill of Sion is a fair place, and the joy of the whole earth
verses.second: upon the northſide lieth the city of the great King; God is well known in her palaces as a ſure refuge.

verses.first: For lo, the kings of the earth
verses.second: are gathered, and gone by together.

verses.first: They marvelled to ſee ſuch things
verses.second: they were aſtoniſhed, and ſuddenly caſt down.

verses.first: Fear came there upon them, and ſorrow
verses.second: as upon a woman in her travail.

verses.first: Thou ſhalt break the ſhips of the ſea
verses.second: through the eaſt wind.

verses.first: Like as we have heard, ſo have we ſeen in the city of the Lord of hoſts, in the city of our God
verses.second: God upholdeth the ſame for ever.

verses.first: We wait for thy loving-kindneſs, O God
verses.second: in the midſt of thy temple.

verses.first: O God, according to thy Name, ſo is thy praiſe unto the world’s end
verses.second: thy right hand is full of righteouſneſs.

verses.first: Let the mount Sion rejoice, and the daughters of Judah be glad
verses.second: becauſe of thy judgments.

verses.first: Walk about Sion, and go round about her
verses.second: and tell the towers thereof.

verses.first: Mark well her bulwarks, ſet up her houſes
verses.second: that ye may tell them that come after.

verses.first: For this God is our God for ever and ever
verses.second: he ſhall be our guide unto death.

verses.first: O Hear ye this, all ye people
verses.second: ponder it with your ears, all ye that dwell in the world;

verses.first: High and low, rich and poor
verses.second: one with another.

verses.first: My mouth ſhall ſpeak of wiſdom
verses.second: and my heart ſhall muſe of underſtanding.

verses.first: I will incline mine ear to the parable
verses.second: and ſhew my dark ſpeech upon the harp.

verses.first: Wherefore ſhould I fear in the days of wickedneſs
verses.second: and when the wickedneſs of my heels compaſſeth me round about?

verses.first: There be ſome that put their truſt in their goods
verses.second: and boaſt themſelves in the multitude of their riches.

verses.first: But no man may deliver his brother
verses.second: nor make agreement unto God for him;

verses.first: For it coſt more to redeem their ſouls
verses.second: ſo that he muſt let that alone for ever;

verses.first: Yea, though he live long
verses.second: and ſee not the grave.

verses.first: For he ſeeth that wiſe men alſo die, and periſh together
verses.second: as well as the ignorant and fooliſh, and leave their riches for other.

verses.first: And yet they think that their houſes ſhall continue for ever
verses.second: and that their dwelling-places ſhall endure from one generation to another; and call the lands after their own names.

verses.first: Nevertheleſs, man will not abide in honour
verses.second: ſeeing that he may be compared unto the beaſts that periſh; this is the way of them.

verses.first: This is their fooliſhneſs
verses.second: and their poſterity praiſe their ſaying.

verses.first: They lie in the hell like ſheep, death gnaweth upon them, and the righteous ſhall have domination over them in the morning
verses.second: their beauty ſhall conſume in the ſepulchre out of their dwelling.

verses.first: But God hath delivered my ſoul from the place of hell
verses.second: for he ſhall receive me.

verses.first: Be not thou afraid, though one be made rich
verses.second: or if the glory of his houſe be increaſed;

verses.first: For he ſhall carry nothing away with him when he dieth
verses.second: neither ſhall his pomp follow him.

verses.first: For while he lived, he counted himſelf an happy man
verses.second: and ſo long as thou doeſt well unto thyſelf, men will ſpeak good of thee.

verses.first: He ſhall follow the generation of his fathers
verses.second: and ſhall never ſee light.

verses.first: Man being in honour hath no underſtanding
verses.second: but is compared unto the beaſts that periſh.

verses.first: THE Lord, even the moſt mighty God, hath ſpoken
verses.second: and called the world, from the riſing up of the ſun unto the going down thereof.

verses.first: Out of Sion hath God appeared
verses.second: in perfect beauty.

verses.first: Our God ſhall come, and ſhall not keep ſilence
verses.second: there ſhall go before him a conſuming fire, and a mighty tempeſt ſhall be ſtirred up round about him.

verses.first: He ſhall call the heaven from above
verses.second: and the earth, that he may judge his people.

verses.first: Gather my ſaints together unto me
verses.second: thoſe that have made a covenant with me with ſacrifice.

verses.first: And the heavens ſhall declare his righteouſneſs
verses.second: for God is Judge himſelf.

verses.first: Hear, O my people, and I will ſpeak
verses.second: I myſelf will teſtify againſt thee, O Iſrael; for I am God, even thy God.

verses.first: I will not reprove thee becauſe of thy ſacrifices, or for thy burnt-offerings
verses.second: becauſe they were not alway before me.

verses.first: I will take no bullock out of thine houſe
verses.second: nor he-goat out of thy folds.

verses.first: For all the beaſts of the foreſt are mine
verses.second: and ſo are the cattle upon a thouſand hills.

verses.first: I know all the fowls upon the mountains
verses.second: and the wild beaſts of the field are in my ſight.

verses.first: If I be hungry, I will not tell thee
verses.second: for the whole world is mine, and all that is therein.

verses.first: Thinkeſt thou that I will eat bulls fleſh
verses.second: and drink the blood of goats?

verses.first: Offer unto God thankſgiving
verses.second: and pay thy vows unto the moſt Higheſt.

verses.first: And call upon me in the time of trouble
verses.second: ſo will I hear thee, and thou ſhalt praiſe me.

verses.first: But unto the ungodly ſaid God
verses.second: Why doſt thou preach my laws, and takeſt my covenant in thy mouth;

verses.first: Whereas thou hateſt to be reformed
verses.second: and has caſt my words behind thee?

verses.first: When thou ſaweſt a thief, thou conſentedſt unto him
verses.second: and haſt been partaker with the adulterers.

verses.first: Thou haſt let thy mouth ſpeak wickedneſs
verses.second: and with thy tongue thou haſt ſet forth deceit.

verses.first: Thou ſateſt, and ſpakeſt againſt thy brother
verses.second: yea, and haſt ſlandered thine own mother’s ſon.

verses.first: Theſe things haſt thou done, and I held my tongue, and thou thoughteſt wickedly, that I am even ſuch a one as thyſelf
verses.second: but I will reprove thee, and ſet before thee the things that thou haſt done.

verses.first: O conſider this, ye that forget God
verses.second: leſt I pluck you away, and there be none to deliver you.

verses.first: Who ſo offereth me thanks and praiſe, he honoureth me
verses.second: and to him that ordereth his converſation right will I ſhew the ſalvation of God.

verses.first: HAVE mercy upon me, O God, after thy great goodneſs
verses.second: according to the multitude of thy mercies do away mine offences.

verses.first: Waſh me throughly from my wickedneſs
verses.second: and cleanſe me from my ſin.

verses.first: For I acknowledge my faults
verses.second: and my ſin is ever before me.

verses.first: Againſt thee only have I ſinned, and done this evil in thy ſight
verses.second: that thou mighteſt be juſtified in thy ſaying, and clear when thou art judged.

verses.first: Behold, I was ſhapen in wickedneſs
verses.second: and in ſin hath my mother conceived me.

verses.first: But lo, thou requireſt truth in the inward parts
verses.second: and ſhalt make me to underſtand wiſdom ſecretly.

verses.first: Thou ſhalt purge me with hyſſop, and I ſhall be clean
verses.second: thou ſhalt waſh me, and I ſhall be whiter than ſnow.

verses.first: Thou ſhalt make me hear of joy and gladneſs
verses.second: that the bones which thou haſt broken may rejoice.

verses.first: Turn thy face from my ſins
verses.second: and put out all my miſdeeds.

verses.first: Make me a clean heart, O God
verses.second: and renew a right ſpirit within me.

verses.first: Caſt me not away from thy preſence
verses.second: and take not thy holy Spirit from me.

verses.first: O give me the comfort of thy help again
verses.second: and ſtabliſh me with thy free Spirit.

verses.first: Then ſhall I teach thy ways unto the wicked
verses.second: and ſinners ſhall be converted unto thee.

verses.first: Deliver me from blood-guiltineſs, O God, thou that art the God of my health
verses.second: and my tongue ſhall ſing of thy righteouſneſs.

verses.first: Thou ſhalt open my lips, O Lord
verses.second: and my mouth ſhall ſhew thy praiſe.

verses.first: For thou deſireſt no ſacrifice, elſe would I give it thee
verses.second: but thou delighteſt not in burntofferings.

verses.first: The ſacrifice of God is a troubled ſpirit
verses.second: a broken and contrite heart, O God, ſhalt thou not deſpiſe.

verses.first: O be favourable and gracious unto Sion
verses.second: build thou the walls of Jeruſalem.

verses.first: Then ſhalt thou be pleaſed with the ſacrifice of righteouſneſs, with the burnt-offerings and oblations
verses.second: then ſhall they offer young bullocks upon thine altar.

verses.first: WHY boaſt eſt thou thyſelf, thou tyrant
verses.second: that thou canſt do miſchief;

verses.first: Whereas the goodneſs of God
verses.second: endureth yet daily?

verses.first: Thy tongue imagineth wickedneſs
verses.second: and with lies thou cutteſt like a ſharp raſor.

verses.first: Thou haſt loved unrighteouſneſs more then goodneſs
verses.second: and to talk of lies more than righteouſneſs.

verses.first: Thou haſt loved to ſpeak all words that may do hurt
verses.second: O thou falſe tongue.

verses.first: Therefore ſhall God deſtroy thee for ever
verses.second: he ſhall take thee, and pluck thee out of thy dwelling, and root thee out of the land of the living.

verses.first: The righteous alſo ſhall ſee this, and fear
verses.second: and ſhall laugh him to ſcorn;

verses.first: Lo, this is the man that took not God for his ſtrength
verses.second: but truſted unto the multitude of his riches, and ſtrengthened himſelf in his wickedneſs.

verses.first: As for me, I am like a green olive-tree in the houſe of God
verses.second: my truſt is in the tender mercy of God for ever and ever.

verses.first: I will always give thanks unto thee for that thou haſt done
verses.second: and I will hope in thy Name, for thy ſaints like it well.

verses.first: THE fooliſh body hath ſaid in his heart
verses.second: There is no God.

verses.first: Corrupt are they, and become abominable in their wickedneſs
verses.second: there is none that doeth good.

verses.first: God looked down from heaven upon the children of men
verses.second: to ſee if there were any that would underſtand, and ſeek after God.

verses.first: But they are all gone out of the way, they are altogether become abominable
verses.second: there is alſo none that doeth good, no not one.

verses.first: Are not they without underſtanding, that work wickedneſs
verses.second: eating up my people as if they would eat bread? they have not called upon God.

verses.first: They were afraid where no fear was
verses.second: for God hath broken the bones of him that beſieged thee; thou haſt put them to confuſion, becauſe God hath deſpiſed them.

verses.first: O that the ſalvation were given unto Iſrael out of Sion
verses.second: O that the Lord would deliver his people out of captivity!

verses.first: Then ſhould Jacob rejoice
verses.second: and Iſrael ſhould be right glad.

verses.first: SAVE me, O God, for thy Name’s ſake
verses.second: and avenge me in thy ſtrength.

verses.first: Hear my prayer, O God
verses.second: and hearken unto the words of my mouth.

verses.first: For ſtrangers are riſen up againſt me
verses.second: and tyrants, which have not God before their eyes, ſeek after my ſoul.

verses.first: Behold, God is my helper
verses.second: the Lord is with them that uphold my ſoul.

verses.first: He ſhall reward evil unto mine enemies
verses.second: deſtroy thou them in thy truth.

verses.first: An offering of a free heart will I give thee, and praiſe thy Name, O Lord
verses.second: becauſe it is ſo comfortable.

verses.first: For he hath delivered me out of all my trouble
verses.second: and mine eye hath ſeen his deſire upon mine enemies.

verses.first: HEAR my prayer, O God
verses.second: and hide not thyſelf from my petition.

verses.first: Take heed unto me, and hear me
verses.second: how I mourn in my prayer, and am vexed.

verses.first: The enemy crieth ſo, and the ungodly cometh on ſo faſt
verses.second: for they are minded to do me ſome miſchief; ſo maliciouſly are they ſet againſt me.

verses.first: My heart is diſquieted within me
verses.second: and the fear of death is fallen upon me.

verses.first: Fearfulneſs and trembling are come upon me
verses.second: and an horrible dread hath overwhelmed me.

verses.first: And I ſaid, O that I had wings like a dove
verses.second: for then would I flee away, and be at reſt.

verses.first: Lo, then would I get me away far off
verses.second: and remain in the wilderneſs.

verses.first: I would make haſte to eſcape
verses.second: becauſe of the ſtormy wind and tempeſt.

verses.first: Deſtroy their tongues, O Lord, and divide them
verses.second: for I have ſpied unrighteouſneſs and ſtrife in the city.

verses.first: Day and night they go about within the walls thereof
verses.second: miſchief alſo and ſorrow are in the midſt of it.

verses.first: Wickedneſs is therein
verses.second: deceit and guile go not out of their ſtreets.

verses.first: For it is not an open enemy that hath done me this diſhonour
verses.second: for then I could have borne it.

verses.first: Neither was it mine adverſary, that did magnify himſelf againſt me
verses.second: for then peradventure I would have hid myſelf from him.

verses.first: But it was even thou, my companion
verses.second: my guide, and mine own familiar friend.

verses.first: We took ſweet counſel together
verses.second: and walked in the houſe of God as friends.

verses.first: Let death come haſtily upon them, and let them go down quick into hell
verses.second: for wickedneſs is in their dwellings, and among them.

verses.first: As for me, I will call upon God
verses.second: and the Lord ſhall ſave me.

verses.first: In the evening, and morning, and at noonday will I pray, and that inſtantly
verses.second: and he ſhall hear my voice.

verses.first: It is he that hath delivered my ſoul in peace from the battle that was againſt me
verses.second: for there were many with me.

verses.first: Yea, even God, that endureth for ever, ſhall hear me, and bring them down
verses.second: for they will not turn, nor fear God.

verses.first: He laid his hands upon ſuch as be at peace with him
verses.second: and he brake his covenant.

verses.first: The words of his mouth were ſofter than butter, having war in his heart
verses.second: his words were ſmoother than oil, and yet be they very ſwords.

verses.first: O caſt thy burden upon the Lord, and he ſhall nouriſh thee
verses.second: and ſhall not ſuffer the righteous to fall for ever.

verses.first: And as for them
verses.second: thou, O God, ſhalt bring them into the pit of deſtruction.

verses.first: The blood-thirſty and deceitful men ſhall not live out half their days
verses.second: nevertheleſs, my truſt ſhall be in thee, O Lord.

verses.first: BE merciful unto me, O God, for man goeth about to devour me
verses.second: he is daily fighting, and troubling me.

verses.first: Mine enemies are daily in hand to ſwallow me up
verses.second: for they be many that fight againſt me, O thou moſt Higheſt.

verses.first: Nevertheleſs, though I am ſometime afraid
verses.second: yet put I my truſt in thee.

verses.first: I will praiſe God, becauſe of his word
verses.second: I have put my truſt in God, and will not fear what fleſh can do unto me.

verses.first: They daily miſtake my words
verses.second: all that they imagine, is to do me evil.

verses.first: They hold all together, and keep themſelves cloſe
verses.second: and mark my ſteps, when they lay wait for my ſoul.

verses.first: Shall they eſcape for their wickedneſs
verses.second: thou, O God, in thy diſpleaſure ſhalt caſt them down.

verses.first: Thou telleſt my flittings; put my tears into thy bottle
verses.second: are not theſe things noted in thy book?

verses.first: Whenſoever I call upon thee, then ſhall mine enemies be put to flight
verses.second: this I know, for God is on my ſide.

verses.first: In God’s word I will rejoice
verses.second: in the Lord’s word will I comfort me.

verses.first: Yea, in God have I put my truſt
verses.second: I will not be afraid what man can do unto me.

verses.first: Unto thee, O God, will I pay my vows
verses.second: unto thee will I give thanks.

verses.first: For thou haſt delivered my ſoul from death, and my feet from falling
verses.second: that I may walk before God in the light of the living.

verses.first: BE merciful unto me, O God, be merciful unto me, for my ſoul truſteth in thee
verses.second: and under the ſhadow of thy wings ſhall be my refuge, until this tyranny be over-paſt.

verses.first: I will call unto the moſt high God
verses.second: even unto the God that ſhall perform the cauſe which I have in hand.

verses.first: He ſhall ſend from heaven
verses.second: and ſave me from the reproof of him that would eat me up.

verses.first: God ſhall ſend forth his mercy and truth
verses.second: my ſoul is among lions.

verses.first: And I lie even among the children of men, that are ſet on fire
verses.second: whoſe teeth are ſpears and arrows, and their tongue a ſharp ſword.

verses.first: Set up thyſelf, O God, above the heavens
verses.second: and thy glory above all the earth.

verses.first: They have laid a net for my feet, and preſſed down my ſoul
verses.second: they have digged a pit before me, and are fallen into the midſt of it themſelves.

verses.first: My heart is fixed, O God, my heart is fixed
verses.second: I will ſing, and give praiſe.

verses.first: Awake up, my glory; awake, lute and harp
verses.second: I myſelf will awake right early.

verses.first: I will give thanks unto thee, O Lord, among the people
verses.second: and I will ſing unto thee among the nations.

verses.first: For the greatneſs of thy mercy reacheth unto the heavens
verses.second: and thy truth unto the clouds.

verses.first: Set up thyſelf, O God, above the heavens
verses.second: and thy glory above all the earth.

verses.first: ARE your minds ſet upon righteouſneſs, O ye congregation
verses.second: and do ye judge the thing that is right, O ye ſons of men?

verses.first: Yea, ye imagine miſchief in your heart upon the earth
verses.second: and your hands deal with wickedneſs.

verses.first: The ungodly are froward, even from their mother’s womb
verses.second: as ſoon as they are born, they go aſtray, and ſpeak lies.

verses.first: They are as venomous as the poiſon of a ſerpent
verses.second: even like the deaf adder that ſtoppeth her ears;

verses.first: Which refuſeth to hear the voice of the charmer
verses.second: charm he never ſo wiſely.

verses.first: Break their teeth, O God, in their mouths; ſmite the jaw-bones of the lions, O Lord
verses.second: let them fall away like water that runneth apace; and when they ſhoot their arrows let them be rooted out.

verses.first: Let them conſume away like a ſnail, and be like the untimely fruit of a woman
verses.second: and let them not ſee the ſun.

verses.first: Or ever your pots be made hot with thorns
verses.second: ſo let indignation vex him, even as a thing that is raw.

verses.first: The righteous ſhall rejoice when he ſeeth the vengeance
verses.second: he ſhall waſh his footſteps in the blood of the ungodly.

verses.first: So that a man ſhall ſay, Verily there is a reward for the righteous
verses.second: doubtleſs there is a God that judgeth the earth.

verses.first: DELIVER me from mine enemies, O God
verses.second: defend me from them that riſe up againſt me.

verses.first: O deliver me from the wicked doers
verses.second: and ſave me from the blood-thirſty men.

verses.first: For lo, they lie waiting for my ſoul
verses.second: the mighty men are gathered againſt me, without any offence or fault of me, O Lord.

verses.first: They run and prepare themſelves without my fault
verses.second: ariſe thou therefore to help me, and behold.

verses.first: Stand up, O Lord God of hoſts, thou God of Iſrael, to viſit all the heathen
verses.second: and be not merciful unto them that offend of malicious wickedneſs.

verses.first: They go to and fro in the evening
verses.second: they grin like a dog, and run about through the city.

verses.first: Behold, they ſpeak with their mouth, and ſwords are in their lips
verses.second: for who doth hear?

verses.first: But thou. O Lord, ſhalt have them in deriſion
verses.second: and thou ſhalt laugh all the heathen to ſcorn.

verses.first: My ſtrength will I aſcribe unto thee
verses.second: for thou art the God of my refuge.

verses.first: God ſheweth me his goodneſs plenteouſly
verses.second: and God ſhall let me ſee my deſire upon mine enemies.

verses.first: Slay them not, leſt my people forget it
verses.second: but ſcatter them abroad among the people, and put them down, O Lord, our defence.

verses.first: For the ſin of their mouth, and for the words of their lips, they ſhall be taken in their pride
verses.second: and why? their preaching is of curſing and lies.

verses.first: Conſume them in thy wrath, conſume them, that they may periſh
verses.second: and know that it is God that ruleth in Jacob, and unto the ends of the world.

verses.first: And in the evening they will return
verses.second: grin like a dog, and will go about the city.

verses.first: They will run here and there for meat
verses.second: and grudge if they be not ſatiſfied.

verses.first: As for me, I will ſing of thy power, and will praiſe thy mercy betimes in the morning
verses.second: for thou haſt been my defence and refuge in the day of my trouble.

verses.first: Unto thee, O my ſtrength, will I ſing
verses.second: for thou, O God, art my refuge, and my merciful God.

verses.first: O God, thou haſt caſt us out, and ſcattered us abroad
verses.second: thou haſt alſo been diſpleaſed; O turn thee unto us again.

verses.first: Thou haſt moved the land, and divided it
verses.second: heal the ſores thereof, for it ſhaketh.

verses.first: Thou haſt ſhewed thy people heavy things
verses.second: thou haſt given us a drink of deadly wine.

verses.first: Thou haſt given a token for ſuch as fear thee
verses.second: that they may triumph becauſe of the truth.

verses.first: Therefore were thy beloved delivered
verses.second: help me with thy right hand, and hear me.

verses.first: God hath ſpoken in his holineſs, I will rejoice, and divide Sichem
verses.second: and mete out the valley of Succoth.

verses.first: Gilead is mine, and Manaſſes is mine
verses.second: Ephraim alſo is the ſtrength of my head; Judah is my law-giver;

verses.first: Moab is my waſh-pot; over Edom will I caſt out my ſhoe
verses.second: Philiſtia, be thou glad of me.

verses.first: Who will lead me into the ſtrong city
verses.second: who will bring me into Edom?

verses.first: Haſt not thou caſt us out, O God
verses.second: wilt not thou, O God, go out with our hoſts?

verses.first: O be thou our help in trouble
verses.second: for vain is the help of man.

verses.first: Through God will we do great acts
verses.second: for it is he that ſhall tread down our enemies.

verses.first: HEAR my crying, O God
verses.second: give ear unto my prayer.

verses.first: From the ends of the earth will I call unto thee
verses.second: when my heart is in heavineſs.

verses.first: O ſet me up upon the rock that is higher than I
verses.second: for thou haſt been my hope, and a ſtrong tower for me againſt the enemy.

verses.first: I will dwell in thy tabernacle for ever
verses.second: and my truſt ſhall be under the covering of thy wings.

verses.first: For thou, O Lord, haſt heard my deſires
verses.second: and haſt given an heritage unto thoſe that fear thy Name.

verses.first: Thou ſhalt grant the king a long life
verses.second: that his years may endure throughout all generations.

verses.first: He ſhall dwell before God for ever
verses.second: O prepare thy loving mercy and faithfulneſs, that they may preſerve him.

verses.first: So will I always ſing praiſe unto thy Name
verses.second: that I may daily perform my vows.

verses.first: MY ſoul truly waiteth ſtill upon God
verses.second: for of him cometh my ſalvation.

verses.first: He verily is my ſtrength and my ſalvation
verses.second: he is my defence, ſo that I ſhall not greatly fall.

verses.first: How long will ye imagine miſchief againſt every man
verses.second: ye ſhall be ſlain all the ſort of you; yea, as a tottering wall ſhall ye be, and like a broken hedge.

verses.first: Their device is only how to put him out whom God will exalt
verses.second: their delight is in lies; they give good words with their mouth, but curſe with their heart.

verses.first: Nevertheleſs, my ſoul, wait thou ſtill upon God
verses.second: for my hope is in him.

verses.first: He truly is my ſtrength and my ſalvation
verses.second: he is my defence, ſo that I ſhall not fall.

verses.first: In God is my health, and my glory
verses.second: the rock of my might, and in God is my truſt.

verses.first: O put your truſt in him alway, ye people
verses.second: pour out your hearts before him, for God is our hope.

verses.first: As for the children of men, they are but vanity
verses.second: the children of men are deceitful upon the weights, they are altogether lighter than vanity itſelf.

verses.first: O truſt not in wrong and robbery, give not yourſelves unto vanity
verses.second: if riches increaſe, ſet not your heart upon them.

verses.first: God ſpake once, and twice I have alſo heard the ſame
verses.second: that power belongeth unto God;

verses.first: And that thou, Lord, art merciful
verses.second: for thou rewardeſt every man according to his work.

verses.first: O God, thou art my God
verses.second: early will I ſeek thee.

verses.first: My ſoul thirſteth for thee, my fleſh alſo longeth after thee
verses.second: in a barren and dry land, where no water is.

verses.first: Thus have I looked for thee in holineſs
verses.second: that I might behold thy power and glory.

verses.first: For thy loving-kindneſs is better than the life itſelf
verses.second: my lips ſhall praiſe thee.

verses.first: As long as I live will I magnify thee on this manner
verses.second: and lift up my hands in thy Name.

verses.first: My ſoul ſhall be ſatiſfied, even as it were with marrow and fatneſs
verses.second: when my mouth praiſeth thee with joyful lips.

verses.first: Have I not remembered thee in my bed
verses.second: and thought upon thee when I was waking? O

verses.first: Becauſe thou haſt been my helper
verses.second: therefore under the ſhadow of thy wings will I rejoice.

verses.first: My ſoul hangeth upon thee
verses.second: thy right hand hath upholden me.

verses.first: Theſe alſo that ſeek the hurt of my ſoul
verses.second: they ſhall go under the earth.

verses.first: Let them fall upon the edge of the ſword
verses.second: that they may be a portion for foxes.

verses.first: But the king ſhall rejoice in God; all they alſo that ſwear by him ſhall be commended
verses.second: for the mouth of them that ſpeak lies ſhall be ſtopped.

verses.first: HEAR my voice, O God, in my prayer
verses.second: preſerve my life from fear of the enemy.

verses.first: Hide me from the gathering together of the froward
verses.second: and from the inſurrection of wicked doers;

verses.first: Who have whet their tongue like a ſword
verses.second: and ſhoot out their arrows, even bitter words;

verses.first: That they may privily ſhoot at him that is perfect
verses.second: ſuddenly do they hit him, and fear not.

verses.first: They encourage themſelves in miſchief
verses.second: and commune among themſelves how they may lay ſnares, and ſay that no man ſhall ſee them.

verses.first: They imagine wickedneſs, and practiſe it
verses.second: that they keep ſecret among themſelves, every man in the deep of his heart.

verses.first: But God ſhall ſuddenly ſhoot at them with a ſwift arrow
verses.second: that they ſhall be wounded.

verses.first: Yea, their own tongues ſhall make them fall
verses.second: inſomuch that who ſo ſeeth them ſhall laugh them to ſcorn.

verses.first: And all men that ſee it ſhall ſay, This hath God done
verses.second: for they ſhall perceive that it is his work.

verses.first: The righteous ſhall rejoice in the Lord, and put his truſt in him
verses.second: and all they that are true of heart ſhall be glad.

verses.first: THOU, O God, art praiſed in Sion
verses.second: and unto thee ſhall the vow be performed in Jeruſalem.

verses.first: Thou that heareſt the prayer
verses.second: unto thee ſhall all fleſh come.

verses.first: My miſdeeds prevail againſt me
verses.second: O be thou merciful unto our ſins.

verses.first: Bleſſed is the man whom thou chooſeſt, and receiveſt unto thee
verses.second: he ſhall dwell in thy court, and ſhall be ſatiſfied with the pleaſures of thy houſe, even of thy holy temple.

verses.first: Thou ſhalt ſhew us wonderful things in thy righteouſneſs, O God of our ſalvation
verses.second: thou that art the hope of all the ends of the earth, and of them that remain in the broad ſea. T

verses.first: Who in his ſtrength ſetteth faſt the mountains
verses.second: and is girded about with power.

verses.first: Who ſtilleth the raging of the ſea
verses.second: and the noiſe of his waves, and the madneſs of the people.

verses.first: They alſo that dwell in the uttermoſt parts of the earth ſhall be afraid at thy tokens
verses.second: thou that makeſt the out-goings of the morning and evening to praiſe thee.

verses.first: Thou viſiteſt the earth, and bleſſeſt it
verses.second: thou makeſt it very plenteous.

verses.first: The river of God is full of water
verses.second: thou prepareſt their corn, for ſo thou provideſt for the earth.

verses.first: Thou watereſt her furrows, thou ſendeſt rain into the little valleys thereof
verses.second: thou makeſt it ſoft with the drops of rain, and bleſſeſt the increaſe of it.

verses.first: Thou crowneſt the year with thy goodneſs
verses.second: and thy clouds drop fatneſs.

verses.first: They ſhall drop upon the dwellings of the wilderneſs
verses.second: and the little hills ſhall rejoice on every ſide.

verses.first: The folds ſhall be full of ſheep
verses.second: the valleys alſo ſhall ſtand ſo thick with corn, that they ſhall laugh and ſing.

verses.first: O Be joyful in God, all ye lands
verses.second: ſing praiſes unto the honour of his Name, make his praiſe to be glorious.

verses.first: Say unto God, O how wonderful art thou in thy works
verses.second: through the greatneſs of thy power ſhall thine enemies be found liars unto thee.

verses.first: For all the world ſhall worſhip thee
verses.second: ſing of thee, and praiſe thy Name.

verses.first: O come hither, and behold the works of God
verses.second: how wonderful he is in his doing toward the children of men.

verses.first: He turned the ſea into dry land
verses.second: ſo that they went through the water on foot; there did we rejoice thereof.

verses.first: He ruleth with his power for ever; his eyes behold the people
verses.second: and ſuch as will not believe ſhall not be able to exalt themſelves.

verses.first: O praiſe our God, ye people
verses.second: and make the voice of his praiſe to be heard;

verses.first: Who holdeth our ſoul in life
verses.second: and ſuffereth not our feet to ſlip.

verses.first: For thou, O God, haſt proved us
verses.second: thou alſo haſt tried us, like as ſilver is tried.

verses.first: Thou broughteſt us into the ſnare
verses.second: and laideſt trouble upon our loins.

verses.first: Thou ſufferedſt men to ride over our heads
verses.second: we went through fire and water, and thou broughteſt us out into a wealthy place.

verses.first: I will go into thine houſe with burntofferings
verses.second: and will pay thee my vows, which I promiſed with my lips, and ſpake with my mouth, when I was in trouble.

verses.first: I will offer unto thee fat burntſacrifices, with the incenſe of rams
verses.second: I will offer bullocks and goats.

verses.first: O come hither, and hearken, all ye that fear God
verses.second: and I will tell you what he hath done for my ſoul.

verses.first: I called unto him with my mouth
verses.second: and gave him praiſes with my tongue.

verses.first: If I incline unto wickedneſs with mine heart
verses.second: the Lord will not hear me.

verses.first: But God hath heard me
verses.second: and conſidered the voice of my prayer.

verses.first: Praiſed be God, who hath not caſt out my prayer
verses.second: nor turned his mercy from me.

verses.text: GOD be merciful unto us, and bleſs us: and ſhew us the light of his countenance, and be merciful unto us:

verses.first: That thy way may be known upon earth
verses.second: thy ſaving-health among all nations.

verses.first: Let the people praiſe thee, O God
verses.second: yea, let all the people praiſe thee.

verses.first: O let the nations rejoice and be glad
verses.second: for thou ſhalt judge the folk righteouſly, and govern the nations upon earth.

verses.first: Let the people praiſe thee, O God
verses.second: let all the people praiſe thee.

verses.first: Then ſhall the earth bring forth her increaſe
verses.second: and God, even our own God, ſhall give us his bleſſing.

verses.first: God ſhall bleſs us
verses.second: and all the ends of the world ſhall fear him.

verses.first: LET God ariſe, and let his enemies be ſcattered
verses.second: let them alſo that hate him flee before him.

verses.first: Like as the ſmoke vaniſheth, ſo ſhalt thou drive them away
verses.second: and like as wax melteth at the fire, ſo let the ungodly periſh at the preſence of God.

verses.first: But let the righteous be glad and rejoice before God
verses.second: let them alſo be merry and joyful .

verses.first: O ſing unto God, and ſing praiſes unto his Name
verses.second: magnify him that rideth upon the heavens, as it were upon an horſe; praiſe him in his Name JAH, and rejoice before him.

verses.first: He is a father of the fatherleſs, and defendeth the cauſe of the widows
verses.second: even God in his holy habitation.

verses.first: He is the God that maketh men to be of one mind in an houſe, and bringeth the priſoners out of captivity
verses.second: but letteth the runagates continue in ſcarceneſs.

verses.first: O God, when thou wenteſt forth before the people
verses.second: when thou wenteſt through the wilderneſs;

verses.first: The earth ſhook, and the heavens dropped at the preſence of God
verses.second: even as Sinai alſo was moved at the preſence of God, who is the God of Iſrael.

verses.first: Thou, O God, ſenteſt a gracious rain upon thine inheritance
verses.second: and refreſhedſt it when it was weary.

verses.first: Thy congregation ſhall dwell therein
verses.second: for thou, O God, haſt of thy goodneſs prepared for the poor.

verses.first: The Lord gave the word
verses.second: great was the company of the preachers.

verses.first: Kings with their armies did flee, and were diſcomfited
verses.second: and they of the houſehold divided the ſpoil.

verses.first: Though ye have lien among the pots, yet ſhall ye be as the wings of a dove
verses.second: that is covered with ſilver wings, and her feathers like gold.

verses.first: When the Almighty ſcattered kings for their ſake
verses.second: then were they as white as ſnow in Salmon.

verses.first: As the hill of Baſan, ſo is God’s hill
verses.second: even an high hill, as the hill of Baſan.

verses.first: Why hop ye ſo, ye high hills? this is God’s hill, in the which it pleaſeth him to dwell
verses.second: yea, the Lord will abide in it for ever.

verses.first: The chariots of God are twenty thouſand, even thouſands of angels
verses.second: and the Lord is among them, as in the holy place of Sinai.

verses.first: Thou art gone up on high, thou haſt led captivity captive, and received gifts for men
verses.second: yea, even for thine enemies, that the Lord God might dwell among them.

verses.first: Praiſed be the Lord daily
verses.second: even the God who helpeth us, and poureth his benefits upon us.

verses.first: He is our God, even the God of whom cometh ſalvation
verses.second: God is the Lord, by whom we eſcape death.

verses.first: God ſhall wound the head of his enemies
verses.second: and the hairy ſcalp of ſuch a one as goeth on ſtill in his wickedneſs.

verses.first: The Lord hath ſaid, I will bring my people again, as I did from Baſan
verses.second: mine own will I bring again, as I did ſometime from the deep of the ſea.

verses.first: That thy foot may be dipped in the blood of thine enemies
verses.second: and that the tongue of thy dogs may be red through the ſame.

verses.first: It is well ſeen, O God, how thou goeſt
verses.second: how thou, my God and King, goeſt in the ſanctuary.

verses.first: The ſingers go before, the minſtrels follow after
verses.second: in the midſt are the damſels playing with the timbrels.

verses.first: Give thanks, O Iſrael, unto God the Lord in the congregations
verses.second: from the ground of the heart.

verses.first: There is little Benjamin their ruler, and the princes of Judah their counſel
verses.second: the princes of Zabulon, and the princes of Nephthali.

verses.first: Thy God hath ſent forth ſtrength for thee
verses.second: ſtabliſh the thing, O God, that thou haſt wrought in us,

verses.first: For thy temple’s ſake at Jeruſalem
verses.second: ſo ſhall kings bring preſents unto thee.

verses.first: When the company of the ſpear-men, and multitude of the mighty are ſcattered abroad among the beaſts of the people, ſo that they humbly bring pieces of ſilver
verses.second: and when he hath ſcattered the people that delight in war;

verses.text: Then ſhall the princes come out of Eqypt; the Morians land ſhall ſoon ſtretch out her hands unto God.

verses.first: Sing unto God, O ye kingdoms of the earth
verses.second: O ſing praiſes unto the Lord;

verses.first: Who ſitteth in the heavens over all from the beginning
verses.second: lo, he doth ſend out his voice, yea, and that a mighty voice.

verses.first: Aſcribe ye the power to God over Iſrael
verses.second: his worſhip and ſtrength is in the clouds.

verses.first: O God, wonderful art thou in thy holy places
verses.second: even the God of Iſrael, he will give ſtrength and power unto his people; bleſſed be God.

verses.first: SAVE me, O God
verses.second: for the waters are come in, even unto my ſoul.

verses.first: I ſtick faſt in the deep mire, where no ground is
verses.second: I am come into deep waters, ſo that the floods run over me.

verses.first: I am weary of crying; my throat is dry
verses.second: my ſight faileth me for waiting ſo long upon my God.

verses.first: They that hate me without a cauſe are more than the hairs of my head
verses.second: they that are mine enemies, and would deſtroy me guiltleſs, are mighty.

verses.first: I paid them the things that I never took
verses.second: God, thou knoweſt my ſimpleneſs, and my faults are not hid from thee.

verses.first: Let not them that truſt in thee, O Lord God of hoſts, be aſhamed for my cauſe
verses.second: let not thoſe that ſeek thee be confounded through me, O Lord God of Iſrael.

verses.first: And why? for thy ſake have I ſuffered reproof
verses.second: ſhame hath covered my face.

verses.first: I am become a ſtranger unto my brethren
verses.second: even an alien unto my mother’s children.

verses.first: For the zeal of thine houſe hath even eaten me
verses.second: and the rebukes of them that rebuked thee are fallen upon me.

verses.first: I wept, and chaſtened myſelf with faſting
verses.second: and that was turned to my reproof.

verses.first: I put on ſackcloth alſo
verses.second: and they jeſted upon me.

verses.first: They that ſit in the gate ſpeak againſt me
verses.second: and the drunkards make ſongs upon me.

verses.first: But, Lord, I make my prayer unto thee
verses.second: in an acceptable time.

verses.first: Hear me, O God, in the multitude of thy mercy
verses.second: even in the truth of thy ſalvation.

verses.first: Take me out of the mire, that I ſink not
verses.second: O let me be delivered from them that hate me, and out of the deep waters.

verses.first: Let not the water-flood drown me, neither let the deep ſwallow me up
verses.second: and let not the pit ſhut her mouth upon me.

verses.first: Hear me, O Lord, for thy loving-kindneſs is comfortable
verses.second: turn thee unto me according to the multitude of thy mercies.

verses.first: And hide not thy face from thy ſervant, for I am in trouble
verses.second: O haſte thee, and hear me.

verses.first: Draw nigh unto my ſoul, and ſave it
verses.second: O deliver me, becauſe of mine enemies.

verses.first: Thou haſt known my reproof, my ſhame, and my diſhonour
verses.second: mine adverſaries are all in thy ſight.

verses.first: Thy rebuke hath broken my heart; I am full of heavineſs
verses.second: I looked for ſome to have pity on me, but there was no man, neither found I any to comfort me.

verses.first: They gave me gall to eat
verses.second: and when I was thirſty they gave me vinegar to drink.

verses.first: Let their table be made a ſnare to take themſelves withal
verses.second: and let the things that ſhould have been for their wealth be unto them an occaſion of falling.

verses.first: Let their eyes be blinded, that they ſee not
verses.second: and ever bow thou down their backs.

verses.first: Pour out thine indignation upon them
verses.second: and let thy wrathful diſpleaſure take hold of them.

verses.first: Let their habitation be void
verses.second: and no man to dwell in their tents.

verses.first: For they perſecute him whom thou haſt ſmitten
verses.second: and they talk how they may vex them whom thou haſt wounded.

verses.first: Let them fall from one wickedneſs to another
verses.second: and not come into thy righteouſneſs.

verses.first: Let them be wiped out of the book of the living
verses.second: and not be written among the righteous.

verses.first: As for me, when I am poor and in heavineſs
verses.second: thy help, O God, ſhall lift me up.

verses.first: I will praiſe the Name of God with a ſong
verses.second: and magnify it with thankſgiving.

verses.first: This alſo ſhall pleaſe the Lord
verses.second: better than a bullock that hath horns and hoofs.

verses.first: The humble ſhall conſider this, and be glad
verses.second: ſeek ye after God, and your ſoul ſhall live.

verses.first: For the Lord heareth the poor
verses.second: and deſpiſeth not his priſoners.

verses.first: Let heaven and earth praiſe him
verses.second: the ſea, and all that moveth therein.

verses.first: For God will ſave Sion, and build the cities of Judah
verses.second: that men may dwell there, and have it in poſſeſſion.

verses.first: The poſterity alſo of his ſervants ſhall inherit it
verses.second: and they that love his Name ſhall dwell therein.

verses.first: HASTE thee, O God, to deliver me
verses.second: make haſte to help me, O Lord.

verses.first: Let them be aſhamed and confounded that ſeek after my ſoul
verses.second: let them be turned backward and put to confuſion that wiſh me evil.

verses.first: Let them for their reward be ſoon brought to ſhame
verses.second: that cry over me, There, there.

verses.first: But let all thoſe that ſeek thee be joyful and glad in thee
verses.second: and let all ſuch as delight in thy ſalvation ſay alway, The Lord be praiſed.

verses.first: As for me, I am poor and in miſery
verses.second: haſte thee unto me, O God.

verses.first: Thou art my helper and my redeemer
verses.second: O Lord, make no long tarrying.

verses.first: IN thee, O Lord, have I put my truſt, let me never be put to confuſion
verses.second: but rid me, and deliver me in thy righteouſneſs; incline thine ear unto me, and ſave me.

verses.first: Be thou my ſtrong hold, whereunto I may alway reſort
verses.second: thou haſt promiſed to help me, for thou art my houſe of defence and my caſtle.

verses.first: Deliver me, O my God, out of the hand of the ungodly
verses.second: out of the hand of the unrighteous and cruel man.

verses.first: For thou, O Lord God, art the thing that I long for
verses.second: thou art my hope, even from my youth.

verses.first: Through thee have I been holden up ever ſince I was born
verses.second: thou art he that took me out of my mother’s womb; my praiſe ſhall be always of thee.

verses.first: I am become as it were a monſter unto many
verses.second: but my ſure truſt is in thee.

verses.first: O let my mouth be filled with thy praiſe
verses.second: that I may ſing of thy glory and honour all the day long.

verses.first: Caſt me not away in the time of age
verses.second: forſake me not when my ſtrength faileth me.

verses.first: For mine enemies ſpeak againſt me, and they that lay wait for my ſoul take their counſel together, ſaying
verses.second: God hath forſaken him; perſecute him, and take him, for there is none to deliver him.

verses.first: Go not far from me, O God
verses.second: my God, haſte thee to help me.

verses.first: Let them be confounded and periſh that are againſt my ſoul
verses.second: let them be covered with ſhame and diſhonour that ſeek to do me evil.

verses.first: As for me, I will patiently abide alway
verses.second: and will praiſe thee more and more.

verses.first: My mouth ſhall daily ſpeak of thy righteouſneſs and ſalvation
verses.second: for I know no end thereof.

verses.first: I will go forth in the ſtrength of the Lord God
verses.second: and will make mention of thy righteouſneſs only.

verses.first: Thou, O God, haſt taught me from my youth up until now
verses.second: therefore will I tell of thy wondrous works.

verses.first: Forſake me not, O God, in mine old age, when I am gray-headed
verses.second: until I have ſhewed thy ſtrength unto this generation, and thy power to all them that are yet for to come.

verses.first: Thy righteouſneſs, O God, is very high
verses.second: and great things are they that thou haſt done; O God, who is like unto thee?

verses.first: O what great troubles and adverſities haſt thou ſhewed me! and yet didſt thou turn and refreſh me
verses.second: yea, and broughteſt me from the deep of the earth again.

verses.first: Thou haſt brought me to great honour
verses.second: and comforted me on every ſide.

verses.first: Therefore will I praiſe thee and thy faithfulneſs, O God, playing upon an inſtrument of muſick
verses.second: unto thee will I ſing upon the harp, O thou Holy One of Iſrael.

verses.first: My lips will be fain when I ſing unto thee
verses.second: and ſo will my ſoul whom thou haſt delivered.

verses.first: My tongue alſo ſhall talk of thy righteouſneſs all the day long
verses.second: for they are confounded and brought unto ſhame that ſeek to do me evil.

verses.first: GIVE the King thy judgments, O God
verses.second: and thy righteouſneſs unto the king's ſon.

verses.first: Then ſhall he judge thy people according unto right
verses.second: and defend the poor.

verses.first: The mountains alſo ſhall bring peace
verses.second: and the little hills righteouſneſs unto the people.

verses.first: He ſhall keep the ſimple folk by their right
verses.second: defend the children of the poor, and puniſh the wrong-doer.

verses.first: They ſhall fear thee, as long as the ſun and moon endureth
verses.second: from one generation to another.

verses.first: He ſhall come down like the rain into a fleece of wool
verses.second: even as the drops that water the earth.

verses.first: In his time ſhall the righteous flouriſh
verses.second: yea, and abundance of peace, ſo long as the moon endureth.

verses.first: His dominion ſhall be alſo from the one ſea to the other
verses.second: and from the flood unto the world’s end.

verses.first: They that dwell in the wilderneſs ſhall kneel before him
verses.second: his enemies ſhall lick the duſt.

verses.first: The kings of Tharſis and of the iſles ſhall give preſents
verses.second: the kings of Arabia and Saba ſhall bring gifts.

verses.first: All kings ſhall fall down before him
verses.second: all nations ſhall do him ſervice.

verses.first: For he ſhall deliver the poor when he crieth
verses.second: the needy alſo, and him that hath no helper.

verses.first: He ſhall be favourable to the ſimple and needy
verses.second: and ſhall preſerve the ſouls of the poor.

verses.first: He ſhall deliver their ſouls from falſehood and wrong
verses.second: and dear ſhall their blood be in his ſight.

verses.first: He ſhall live, and unto him ſhall be given of the gold of Arabia
verses.second: prayer ſhall be made ever unto him, and daily ſhall he be praiſed.

verses.first: There ſhall be an heap of corn in the earth, high upon the hills
verses.second: his fruit ſhall ſhake like Libanus, and ſhall be green in the city like graſs upon the earth.

verses.first: His Name ſhall endure for ever; his Name ſhall remain under the ſun among the poſterities
verses.second: which ſhall be bleſſed through him; and all the heathen ſhall praiſe him.

verses.first: Bleſſed be the Lord God, even the God of Iſrael
verses.second: which only doeth wondrous things;

verses.first: And bleſſed be the Name of his majeſty for ever
verses.second: and all the earth ſhall be filled with his majeſty. Amen, Amen.

verses.first: TRULY God is loving unto Iſrael
verses.second: even unto ſuch as are of a clean heart.

verses.first: Nevertheleſs, my feet were almoſt gone
verses.second: my treadings had well-nigh ſlipt.

verses.first: And why? I was grieved at the wicked
verses.second: I do alſo ſee the ungodly in ſuch proſperity.

verses.first: For they are in no peril of death
verses.second: but are luſty and ſtrong.

verses.first: They come in no miſfortune like other folk
verses.second: neither are they plagued like other men.

verses.first: And this is the cauſe that they are ſo holden with pride
verses.second: and overwhelmed with cruelty.

verses.first: Their eyes ſwell with fatneſs
verses.second: and they do even what they luſt.

verses.first: They corrupt other, and ſpeak of wicked blaſphemy
verses.second: their talking is againſt the moſt High.

verses.first: For they ſtretch forth their mouth unto the heaven
verses.second: and their tongue goeth through the world.

verses.first: Therefore fall the people unto them
verses.second: and thereout ſuck they no ſmall advantage.

verses.first: Tuſh, ſay they, how ſhould God perceive it
verses.second: is there knowledge in the moſt High?

verses.first: Lo, theſe are the ungodly, theſe proſper in the world, and theſe have riches in poſſeſſion
verses.second: and I ſaid, Then have I cleanſed my heart in vain, and waſhed mine hands in innocency.

verses.first: All the day long have I been puniſhed
verses.second: and chaſtened every morning.

verses.first: Yea, and I had almoſt ſaid even as they
verses.second: but lo, then I ſhould have condemned the generation of thy children.

verses.first: Then thought I to underſtand this
verses.second: but it was too hard for me;

verses.first: Until I went into the ſanctuary of God
verses.second: then underſtood I the end of theſe men;

verses.first: Namely, how thou doſt ſet them in ſlippery places
verses.second: and caſt eſt them down, and deſtroyeſt them.

verses.first: O how ſuddenly do they conſume
verses.second: periſh, and come to a fearful end!

verses.first: Yea, even like as a dream when one awaketh
verses.second: ſo ſhalt thou make their image to vaniſh out of the city.

verses.first: Thus my heart was grieved
verses.second: and it went even through my reins.

verses.first: So fooliſh was I, and ignorant
verses.second: even as it were a beaſt before thee.

verses.first: Nevertheleſs, I am alway by thee
verses.second: for thou haſt holden me by my right hand.

verses.first: Thou ſhalt guide me with thy counſel
verses.second: and after that receive me with glory.

verses.first: Whom have I in heaven but thee
verses.second: and there is none upon earth that I deſire in compariſon of thee.

verses.first: My fleſh and my heart faileth
verses.second: but God is the ſtrength of my heart, and my portion for ever.

verses.first: For lo, they that forſake thee ſhall periſh
verses.second: thou haſt deſtroyed all them that commit fornication againſt thee.

verses.first: But it is good for me to hold me faſt by God, to put my truſt in the Lord God
verses.second: and to ſpeak of all thy works in the gates of the daughter of Sion.

verses.first: O God, wherefore art thou abſent from us ſo long
verses.second: why is thy wrath ſo hot againſt the ſheep of thy paſture?

verses.first: O think upon thy congregation
verses.second: whom thou haſt purchaſed and redeemed of old.

verses.first: Think upon the tribe of thine inheritance
verses.second: and mount Sion, wherein thou haſt dwelt.

verses.first: Lift up thy feet, that thou mayeſt utterly deſtroy every enemy
verses.second: which hath done evil in thy ſanctuary.

verses.first: Thine adverſaries roar in the midſt of thy congregations
verses.second: and ſet up their banners for tokens.

verses.first: He that hewed timber afore out of the thick trees
verses.second: was known to bring it to an excellent work.

verses.first: But now they break down all the carved work thereof
verses.second: with axes and hammers.

verses.first: They have ſet fire upon thy holy places
verses.second: and have defiled the dwelling-place of thy Name, even unto the ground.

verses.first: Yea, they ſaid in their hearts, Let us make havock of them altogether
verses.second: thus have they burnt up all the houſes of God in the land.

verses.first: We ſee not our tokens, there is not one prophet more
verses.second: no, not one is there among us, that underſtandeth any more.

verses.first: O God, how long ſhall the adverſary do this diſhonour
verses.second: how long ſhall the enemy blaſpheme thy Name, for ever?

verses.first: Why withdraweſt thou thy hand
verses.second: why pluckeſt thou not thy right hand out of thy boſom to conſume the enemy?

verses.first: For God is my King of old
verses.second: the help that is done upon earth he doeth it himſelf.

verses.first: Thou didſt divide the ſea through thy power
verses.second: thou brakeſt the heads of the dragons in the waters.

verses.first: Thou ſmoteſt the heads of Leviathan in pieces
verses.second: and gaveſt him to be meat for the people in the wilderneſs.

verses.first: Thou broughteſt out fountains and waters out of the hard rocks
verses.second: thou driedſt up mighty waters.

verses.first: The day is thine, and the night is thine
verses.second: thou haſt prepared the light, and the ſun.

verses.first: Thou haſt ſet all the borders of the earth
verses.second: thou haſt made ſummer and winter.

verses.first: Remember this, O Lord, how the enemy hath rebuked
verses.second: and how the fooliſh people hath blaſphemed thy Name.

verses.first: O deliver not the ſoul of thy turtle-dove unto the multitude of the enemies
verses.second: and forget not the congregation of the poor for ever.

verses.first: Look upon the covenant
verses.second: for all the earth is full of darkneſs and cruel habitations.

verses.first: O let not the ſimple go away aſhamed
verses.second: but let the poor and needy give praiſe unto thy Name.

verses.first: Ariſe, O God, maintain thine own cauſe
verses.second: remember how the fooliſh man blaſphemeth thee daily.

verses.first: Forget not the voice of thine enemies
verses.second: the preſumption of them that hate thee increaſeth ever more and more.

verses.first: UNTO thee, O God, do we give thanks
verses.second: yea, unto thee do we give thanks.

verses.first: Thy Name alſo is ſo nigh
verses.second: and that do thy wondrous works declare.

verses.first: When I receive the congregation
verses.second: I ſhall judge according unto right.

verses.first: The earth is weak, and all the inhabiters thereof
verses.second: I bear up the pillars of it.

verses.first: I ſaid unto the fools, Deal not ſo madly
verses.second: and to the ungodly, Set not up your horn;

verses.first: Set not up your horn on high
verses.second: and ſpeak not with a ſtiff neck.

verses.first: For promotion cometh neither from the eaſt, nor from the weſt
verses.second: nor yet from the ſouth.

verses.first: And why? God is the Judge
verses.second: he putteth down one, and ſetteth up another.

verses.first: For in the hand of the Lord there is a cup, and the wine is red
verses.second: it is full mixed, and he poureth out of the ſame.

verses.first: As for the dregs thereof
verses.second: all the ungodly of the earth ſhall drink them, and ſuck them out.

verses.first: But I will talk of the God of Jacob
verses.second: and praiſe him for ever.

verses.first: All the horns of the ungodly alſo will I break
verses.second: and the horns of the righteous ſhall be exalted.

verses.first: IN Jewry is God known
verses.second: his Name is great in Iſrael.

verses.first: At Salem is his tabernacle
verses.second: and his dwelling in Sion.

verses.first: There brake he the arrows of the bow
verses.second: the ſhield, the ſword, and the battle.

verses.first: Thou art of more honour and might
verses.second: than the hills of the robbers.

verses.first: The proud are robbed, they have ſlept their ſleep
verses.second: and all the men whoſe hands were mighty, have found nothing.

verses.first: At thy rebuke, O God of Jacob
verses.second: both the chariot and horſe are fallen.

verses.first: Thou, even thou art to be feared
verses.second: and who may ſtand in thy ſight when thou art angry?

verses.first: Thou didſt cauſe thy judgment to be heard from heaven
verses.second: the earth trembled, and was ſtill,

verses.first: When God aroſe to judgment
verses.second: and to help all the meek upon earth.

verses.first: The fierceneſs of man ſhall turn to thy praiſe
verses.second: and the fierceneſs of them ſhalt thou refrain.

verses.first: Promiſe unto the Lord your God, and keep it, all ye that are round about him
verses.second: bring preſents unto him that ought to be feared.

verses.first: He ſhall refrain the ſpirit of princes
verses.second: and is wonderful among the kings of the earth.

verses.first: I Will cry unto God with my voice
verses.second: even unto God will I cry with my voice, and he ſhall hearken unto me.

verses.first: In the time of my trouble I ſought the Lord
verses.second: my ſore ran and ceaſed not in the nightſeaſon ; my ſoul refuſed comfort.

verses.first: When I am in heavineſs, I will think upon God
verses.second: when my heart is vexed, I will complain.

verses.first: Thou holdeſt mine eyes waking
verses.second: I am ſo feeble, that I cannot ſpeak.

verses.first: I have conſidered the days of old
verses.second: and the years that are paſt.

verses.first: I call to remembrance my ſong
verses.second: and in the night I commune with mine own heart, and ſearch out my ſpirits.

verses.first: Will the Lord abſent himſelf for ever
verses.second: and will he be no more intreated?

verses.first: Is his mercy clean gone for ever
verses.second: and is his promiſe come utterly to an end for evermore?

verses.first: Hath God forgotten to be gracious
verses.second: and will he ſhut up his loving-kindneſs in diſpleaſure?

verses.first: And I ſaid, It is mine own infirmity
verses.second: but I will remember the years of the right hand of the moſt Higheſt.

verses.first: I will remember the works of the Lord
verses.second: and call to mind thy wonders of old time.

verses.first: I will think alſo of all thy works
verses.second: and my talking ſhall be of thy doings.

verses.first: Thy way, O God, is holy
verses.second: who is ſo great a God as our God?

verses.first: Thou art the God that doeth wonders
verses.second: and haſt declared thy power among the people.

verses.first: Thou haſt mightily delivered thy people
verses.second: even the ſons of Jacob and Joſeph.

verses.first: The waters ſaw thee, O God, the waters ſaw thee, and were afraid
verses.second: the depths alſo were troubled.

verses.first: The clouds poured out water, the air thundered
verses.second: and thine arrows went abroad.

verses.first: The voice of thy thunder was heard round about
verses.second: the lightnings ſhone upon the ground; the earth was moved, and ſhook withal.

verses.first: Thy way is in the ſea, and thy paths in the great waters
verses.second: and thy footſteps are not known.

verses.first: Thou leddeſt thy people like ſheep
verses.second: by the hand of Moſes and Aaron.

verses.first: HEAR my law, O my people
verses.second: incline your ears unto the words of my mouth.

verses.first: I will open my mouth in a parable
verses.second: I will declare hard ſentences of old;

verses.first: Which we have heard and known
verses.second: and ſuch as our fathers have told us;

verses.first: That we ſhould not hide them from the children of the generations to come
verses.second: but to ſhew the honour of the Lord, his mighty and wonderful works that he hath done.

verses.first: He made a covenant with Jacob, and gave Iſrael a law
verses.second: which he commanded our forefathers to teach their children;

verses.first: That their poſterity might know it
verses.second: and the children which were yet unborn;

verses.first: To the intent that when they came up
verses.second: they might ſhew their children the ſame;

verses.first: That they might put their truſt in God
verses.second: and not to forget the works of God, but to keep his commandments;

verses.first: And not to be as their forefathers, a faithleſs and ſtubborn generation
verses.second: a generation that ſet not their heart aright, and whoſe ſpirit cleaveth not ſtedfaſtly unto God;

verses.first: Like as the children of Ephraim
verses.second: who being harneſſed, and carrying bows, turned themſelves back in the day of battle.

verses.first: They kept not the covenant of God
verses.second: and would not walk in his law;

verses.first: But forgat what he had done
verses.second: and the wonderful works that he had ſhewed for them.

verses.first: Marvellous things did he in the ſight of our forefathers, in the land of Egypt
verses.second: even in the field of Zoan.

verses.first: He divided the ſea, and let them go through
verses.second: he made the waters to ſtand on an heap.

verses.first: In the day-time alſo he led them with a cloud
verses.second: and all the night through with a light of fire.

verses.first: He clave the hard rocks in the wilderneſs
verses.second: and gave them drink thereof, as it had been out of the great depth.

verses.first: He brought waters out of the ſtony rock
verses.second: ſo that it guſhed out like the rivers.

verses.first: Yet for all this they ſinned more againſt him
verses.second: and provoked the moſt Higheſt in the wilderneſs.

verses.first: They tempted God in their hearts
verses.second: and required meat for their luſt.

verses.first: They ſpake againſt God alſo, ſaying
verses.second: Shall God prepare a table in the wilderneſs?

verses.first: He ſmote the ſtony rock indeed, that the waters guſhed out, and the ſtreams flowed withal
verses.second: but can he give bread alſo, or provide fleſh for his people?

verses.first: When the Lord heard this, he was wroth
verses.second: ſo the fire was kindled in Jacob, and there came up heavy diſpleaſure againſt Iſrael;

verses.first: Becauſe they believed not in God
verses.second: and put not their truſt in his help.

verses.first: So he commanded the clouds above
verses.second: and opened the doors of heaven.

verses.first: He rained down Manna alſo upon them for to eat
verses.second: and gave them food from heaven.

verses.first: So man did eat angels food
verses.second: for he ſent them meat enough.

verses.first: He cauſed the eaſt-wind to blow under heaven
verses.second: and through his power he brought in the ſouth-weſt-wind.

verses.first: He rained fleſh upon them as thick as duſt
verses.second: and feathered fowls like as the ſand of the ſea.

verses.first: He let it fall among their tents
verses.second: even round about their habitation.

verses.first: So they did eat and were well filled, for he gave them their own deſire
verses.second: they were not diſappointed of their luſt.

verses.first: But while the meat was yet in their mouths, the heavy wrath of God came upon them, and ſlew the wealthieſt of them
verses.second: yea, and ſmote down the choſen men that were in Iſrael.

verses.first: But for all this they ſinned yet more
verses.second: and believed not his wondrous works.

verses.first: Therefore their days did he conſume in vanity
verses.second: and their years in trouble.

verses.first: When he ſlew them, they ſought him
verses.second: and turned them early, and inquired after God.

verses.first: And they remembered that God was their ſtrength
verses.second: and that the high God was their redeemer.

verses.first: Nevertheleſs, they did but flatter him with their mouth
verses.second: and diſſembled with him in their tongue.

verses.first: For their heart was not whole with him
verses.second: neither continued they ſtedfaſt in his covenant.

verses.first: But he was ſo merciful, that he forgave their miſdeeds
verses.second: and deſtroyed them not.

verses.first: Yea, many a time turned he his wrath away
verses.second: and would not ſuffer his whole diſpleaſure to ariſe.

verses.first: For he conſidered that they were but fleſh
verses.second: and that they were even a wind that paſſeth away, and cometh not again.

verses.first: Many a time did they provoke him in the wilderneſs
verses.second: and grieved him in the deſert.

verses.first: They turned back, and tempted God
verses.second: and moved the Holy One in Iſrael.

verses.first: They thought not of his hand
verses.second: and of the day when he delivered them from the hand of the enemy;

verses.first: How he had wrought his miracles in Egypt
verses.second: and his wonders in the field of Zoan.

verses.first: He turned their waters into blood
